sourceEvidence.label: Mainframe release authority current working-tree evidence

assessment.summary: The current release bytes are strongly checked, but signing and publication authority must move out of the tag-controlled workflow before those checks can authorize a public release.

nonNegotiables: Candidate or tag-controlled code must not execute in a job with signing or publication authority.
The 16 tested candidate assets must cross the boundary without being rebuilt.
The protected release environment and prepublication draft-byte verification must remain.
Existing immutable releases must be verified against their original receipt and provenance rather than current rerun bytes.
The migration must not change the Mainframe runtime archive solely because of workflow or test changes.
assumptions: The protected default branch is a trusted control boundary for release workflow definitions.
No measured release latency, memory, or API-call budget was supplied.
PyPI publication is outside this hardening decision.
A separately scoped policy credential or external prerequisite remains available for immutable-release policy inspection.

opportunities.title: Separate release authority from candidate code
opportunities.summary: Turn the tag workflow into an unprivileged evidence producer and move signing and publication into certificate-distinct default-branch workflows.
opportunities.diagnosis: Release bytes are bound precisely, but the same tag-selected workflow can execute repository code and mint attestations, while its write-capable publisher checks out and executes the release commit. The authority boundary therefore does not independently identify the program that certified and published the bytes.

evidence.claim: The release-build path executes repository-controlled code with OIDC and attestation-write permissions, and release-publish executes the release commit with contents-write authority.
Focused workflow coverage locks exact asset inventory, tag identity, provenance subjects, draft-byte checks, and immutable-release rerun behavior.
MCP package coverage binds the wheel, source distribution, runtime pair, and persistent pipx install path to the tested runtime candidate.

Because multiple code-executing jobs share the tag workflow's provenance and dangerous permissions, workflow identity alone cannot establish that only an intended clean signer minted a release-authorizing statement.

A workflow_run consumer can receive write authority after an unprivileged producer, its definition comes from the default branch, untrusted artifacts require defensive handling, and a chain is limited to three workflow levels.
Attestation verification can restrict an exact signer workflow, allowing a dedicated signer path to be certificate-distinguishable from the candidate workflow.
Artifact and release APIs expose stable IDs, source-run metadata, sizes, and SHA-256 digests for a fail-closed handoff.
A workflow run ID survives reruns while the run attempt increments, and artifact metadata does not independently bind an artifact to that attempt.
Release-asset immutability begins only after publication, so exact draft inventory and downloaded-byte verification must complete before publication.
Repository immutable-release policy inspection requires Administration read and should not broaden the write-capable publisher's repository token.

desiredInvariants: No job that checks out or executes candidate or tag-controlled code has OIDC, attestation-write, artifact-metadata-write, protected release secrets, or contents-write permission.
Every release-authorizing statement is certificate-distinguishable from every code-executing candidate job.
The only contents-write job runs protected default-branch workflow code, performs no checkout, and treats downloaded bytes solely as untrusted data.

A canonical signing request and signer-produced authorization receipt bind producer and signer runs and attempts, raw tag and peeled commit identities, artifact IDs and API digests, and every release filename, size, and SHA-256.
The public release contains exactly the 16 tested candidate assets plus the signed authorization receipt.
A partial or ambiguous publication remains a reversible draft and never becomes an immutable public release.
An existing immutable release is verification-only and is checked against its own original authorization receipt and signer provenance.

options.title: Retain the tag workflow with stronger local guards
options.summary: Keep the current workflow topology while reducing credential exposure and adding more receipt and ordering checks.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Credential scoping and local guards reduce accidental exposure but do not separate authority from tag-controlled code.
The current exact inventory and draft checks remain useful tactical controls.
The signer remains inside the same workflow identity and is not certificate-distinct.

tradeoffs.assessment: Narrower token exposure and stronger local validation reduce mistakes, but candidate-selected code remains in the release authority domain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Statically enumerate every permission, secret, checkout, and attestation step, then prove a same-workflow code-executing job still shares signer authority.

tradeoffs.assessment: No additional workflow hop or full-packet transfer is required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare candidate-to-publication elapsed time and downloaded bytes with the current workflow.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local guards require only bounded receipt and digest state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak resident memory while validating the fixed asset inventory.

tradeoffs.assessment: More exact checks catch drift earlier, but signing, publishing, and candidate execution still share one blast radius.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject failures before signing, during upload, and before publication and inspect the resulting release state.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing one-workflow operating model remains familiar.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Have a maintainer rehearse the current rerun and partial-draft runbook.

tradeoffs.assessment: The change can be delivered as focused permission and validation edits.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the existing release workflow contract and compare the workflow graph before and after.

residualRisks: Tag-controlled code can still mint provenance and execute under publication authority.
Workflow identity still cannot distinguish the intended signer from another authorized job.

workPackages: Remove persisted credentials and narrow secrets.
Add canonical handoff and step-order assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: Every current byte and draft check remains green.
The option is explicitly documented as non-authorizing temporary hardening.
migrationNotes: Do not use this option to authorize a public 10.2.0 release.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the focused permission and contract-test edits.

options.title: Use default-branch signer and publisher workflows
options.summary: Make the tag workflow an unprivileged producer, then use a default-branch signer and a checkout-free protected publisher as two workflow_run consumers.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Dangerous signing and publication capabilities move out of every candidate-code execution job.
Exact inventory, tag, provenance, draft, and rerun checks are preserved and redistributed by trust stage.
The design uses the documented default-branch privileged-consumer boundary and remains within the three-level workflow_run chain limit.
The release verifier can require the dedicated signer workflow identity rather than test.yml at the tag commit.
Attempt-qualified no-overwrite artifacts plus signed producer and signer attempt fields close rerun substitution.
The publisher verifies exact remote draft bytes before publication and retains verification-only rerun behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: The observed authority overlaps disappear because candidate code has no signing or write capability and the signer and publisher have distinct default-branch workflow identities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prove exact permissions and workflow identities statically, then run hostile-artifact and wrong-signer hosted canaries.

tradeoffs.assessment: Two workflow starts and repeated streaming digest passes add latency and packet I/O to a low-frequency release path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare candidate-to-publication elapsed time, API calls, and bytes transferred against the current tagged workflow; reject unbounded growth.

tradeoffs.assessment: Receipts are capped at 64 KiB and large assets can be hashed in chunks, so the design need not buffer the packet in memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak resident memory in signer and publisher while processing the largest candidate archive.

tradeoffs.assessment: Signing and publishing fail independently, publication remains a reversible draft, and immutable reruns are verification-only; event delivery and cross-run state add new failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject every stage boundary and require deterministic retry, exact partial-draft handling, and zero writes on ambiguous state.

tradeoffs.assessment: Maintainers must correlate producer, signer, and publisher runs and operate a versioned receipt and draft state machine.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse the runbook with a disposable tag and require summaries to expose every run, attempt, artifact, tag, receipt, draft, and recovery identity.

tradeoffs.assessment: The cutover adds two workflows, two canonical control documents, a seventeenth asset, new signer policy, and adversarial state-machine coverage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Land read-only contracts first, canary the chain, then atomically remove all legacy signing and publishing authority before enabling the new publisher.

residualRisks: Protected default-branch compromise or a repository administrator can still alter release policy.
GitHub-hosted runner, OIDC, attestation, or API compromise remains outside this repository control.
A separately scoped immutable-policy credential remains sensitive and must be limited to policy inspection.
This is release authorization, not proof that the signer itself built the candidate under SLSA level 3 semantics.

workPackages: Define canonical signing-request and authorization-receipt contracts.
Remove all signing and publication authority from the candidate workflow.
Add a checkout-free default-branch signer with exact producer and artifact validation.
Add a checkout-free protected publisher with exact statement, tag, draft, and immutable-release validation.
Add static, dynamic, rerun, partial-draft, no-execution, and hosted negative tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Every tag-triggered code-executing job is unprivileged.
Only the signer can mint the dedicated release-authorization statement and only the publisher has contents-write authority.
The signer statement covers exactly the 16 candidate assets plus the authorization receipt.
A hosted disposable tag proves exact signer certificate identity, protected approval, draft-byte verification, and immutable final verification.
No failure or rerun can publish rebuilt, cross-attempt, ambiguous, or partially verified bytes.
migrationNotes: Increase producer artifact retention from 7 days to at least 30 days.
Do not retain a legacy tag-controlled signer or publisher fallback.
A trusted default-branch manual promotion may be the emergency fallback.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the signer and publisher workflows and protected environment entry, preserve evidence and any draft for review, and use trusted default-branch manual verification without restoring tag-controlled authority.

options.title: Move release authority to an external controller
options.summary: Use a separately protected repository or GitHub App to validate, sign, and publish Mainframe release packets.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The Mainframe repository cannot directly change the external controller's release-authority program.
The current byte and draft checks become the cross-system receipt contract.
The controller has an independently managed signer and publisher identity.
Policy introspection and publication permissions can be isolated in a narrowly scoped controller credential.

tradeoffs.assessment: A Mainframe repository compromise cannot directly alter the release-authority code or credential owner.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Demonstrate that Mainframe write access cannot change controller policy, signer identity, or publication credentials.

tradeoffs.assessment: Cross-repository or app delivery adds network hops, API calls, and full-packet transfer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure end-to-end promotion latency and bytes transferred through a controller rehearsal.

tradeoffs.assessment: Streaming validation can keep memory bounded, but controller implementation details are not selected.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require chunked hashing and measure controller peak memory with the largest release packet.

tradeoffs.assessment: Administrative compromise is better contained, while another repository or service adds event-delivery, credential, and availability failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise controller outage, delayed artifact transfer, token rotation, duplicate delivery, and partial-draft recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: A second authority domain needs ownership, access policy, monitoring, credential lifecycle, incident response, and cross-system tracing.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Assign owners and rehearse normal release, credential rotation, emergency disablement, and audit retrieval.

tradeoffs.assessment: The repository, controller, credentials, attestations, receipt protocol, and recovery plan must cut over together.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a parallel nonpublishing controller canary, then remove in-repository authority in one controlled cutover.

residualRisks: The external controller or its administrator becomes a high-value release root of trust.
Cross-system availability and credential lifecycle can delay or block releases.
The same artifact parsing and draft-state protections remain necessary.

workPackages: Select and provision the authority domain.
Define the cross-system receipt and authentication contract.
Implement independent signing, publication, audit, and incident controls.
Canary and cut over without retaining repository-local write authority.
acceptanceCriteria: Mainframe repository write access cannot alter controller policy or credentials.
The controller accepts only exact authenticated packets and publishes only verified drafts.
Cross-system outage and credential-rotation rehearsals have deterministic recovery.
migrationNotes: Choose this option when independent organizational ownership is a non-negotiable requirement.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable controller publication, retain received evidence for review, and use an independently governed emergency release procedure.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the default-branch signer and publisher split under the current single-repository constraints; choose the external controller when protected-default-branch compromise must not be able to change release policy.

openQuestions: Should specialized Pi, MCP, native, and formula statements remain alongside the exact 17-subject release-authorization statement after the first compatible release?
Which protected default-branch revision or ruleset pins the signer and publisher workflow definitions for a release?
Will immutable-release policy be verified by an environment-scoped Administration-read credential or enforced as an external prerequisite?
What reviewed emergency promotion path is available when workflow_run delivery or the protected environment is unavailable?
